chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Upcoming fundraiser at NYU Law School and the membership of the House
summary: The House has about 150 members; young performers and board members like Alan Hanlon will perform.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: full but I'm going to have allot of cooperation. There are allot of parents who'd like to see their kids do something. And listen, I'm working with seniors and they're enjoying it, so you never get too old for music. And the kids, you know, I don't know where they came from or how they got to where they are, so that's what we're going to tell them. I got, I mean all the musicians that I see I tell them what's happening and they say, well call on me so I want to have old models for them, and I want to have guests in and they can talk to them. If these kids are thinking in the wrong direction we just might be able to put them on the right track because the musicians, they paid allot of dues and I think they'd be the first ones to tell them what not to do.

You know the House That Jazz Built has a membership of about 150 people scattered nationally and we have a local board consisting of musicians and people that are especially interested in jazz. We have four jazz parties a year and we have one coming up, Sunday October the 19th. Of course, this is one of the means that we have used to raise funds to carry out the program at The House That Jazz Built. And it's an on-going thing.

So we're looking forward to a good time and one of the young ladies that's going to perform for us, three years ago she worked at The House That Jazz Built under a Jobs For Youth Progam while she was still going to school. And now she's a talent in her own rank. We didn't develop that talent but maybe a little bit of us rubbed off on her. And they call themselves "Born To Be-Bop" and they're going to be doing things . . .

A group, yes. There are seven of them, two girl singers and five musicians. And their repertoire consists of songs by Louie Jordan and Louie Armstrong, so I think that maybe we're getting through to some of them, in all ways.
Yes. That sounds interesting. Who else will be performing?

Well, Alan Hanlon is guitar player. He's one of our Board Members and he's our regular musical director. And the other, young lady with whom I met at one of the performances that I did for the senior citizens, she's got a group of young people and they're going to model fashions. So we hope it's going

to be real great. And I spoke to a friend of mine and I'm keeping my fingers crossed that I think we'll be able to televise this so we'll have something we can show a little later on, about what The House That Jazz Built is really doing. Of course, we have the regulars. I always sing whether anybody asks me or not.
Is it going to be at N.Y.U. Law School?

Yeah, N.Y.U. School of Law. At our last Jazz Party, which was our annual meeting in July, we had Carmen Leggio and Flossie, I forget Flossie's last name, but he plays the tenor and she plays the trumpet and flute. And they're going to play for us. And allot of the musicians from Ryans promised that they would drop in and sit in, so we always have some extra guests. We tell them to bring their axes. And of course we serve a little wine and snacks and have a combination meeting and jazz concert. And the proceeds are used to buy supplies or some of the things we need at The House That Jazz Built, I mean, at this new program because we're not - certain funds are not available for administrative purposes and we'll need to set up some kind of

an administration. So we'll raise the funds ourselves. And there's one thing that I mainly want to do, in the room that we have there's no piano there so we're negotiating for an electronic piano. So the funds that we get from the jazz party will be used for that. That's the main thing we'll get because it has something for the kids. And it has to be portable because the space that we're using, we have to clear in and clear out each time we use it. So a portable piano is just the thing we need.
You're not actually doing this at the House.

No this program will be conducted in a school, Community School 50, in the Bronx, and I have a very nice room and I'll be able to handle 120 kids. Well, there'll be 60 at a time, from seven to fourteen, and 60 from fourteen and a half to nineteen.
